extracted.intended_audience: Federal agencies implementing NEPA, agency counsel, environmental consultants, project sponsors, and public commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Final rule revising CEQ's NEPA implementing regulations (40 CFR parts 1500–1508) to guide how agencies determine level of review, prepare EAs/EISs, engage the public, set page limits and schedules, ensure scientific integrity, resolve disputes, and define key terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose (§1500.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines the purpose of the NEPA implementing regulations and the aims of NEPA implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains NEPA's statutory purpose to promote informed, science‑based decisionmaking and environmental protection for present and future generations; guides agencies to integrate environmental considerations into decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy (§1500.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: States policy principles that should guide agency NEPA implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principles include transparency, informed decisionmaking grounded in science, public engagement, efficiency, and avoidance of unnecessary litigation while allowing agency flexibility to tailor processes to statutory and factual contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA Compliance (§1500.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and standards for when and how agencies must comply with NEPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes circumstances triggering environmental documents, interaction with other laws, and expectations for agencies to interpret and administer policies consistent with NEPA's purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concise and Informative Environmental Documents (§1500.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Environmental documents should be concise and informative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages clarity, brevity, and usefulness of EAs and EISs so they effectively inform decisionmakers and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficient Process (§1500.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: NEPA processes should be efficient and timely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes reducing unnecessary delay and duplication, setting schedules and page limits, and improving regulatory certainty while preserving thorough environmental review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency Authority (§1500.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarifies agencies' discretion and authority in applying NEPA procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes agency-specific statutes and authorities and permits tailoring of NEPA procedures to statutory and programmatic contexts within regulatory bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose (§1501.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose of Part 1501 (NEPA and Agency Planning).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets planning-related aims such as early identification of NEPA requirements and adequate scoping to inform agency decisionmaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine the Appropriate Level of NEPA Review (§1501.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions for choosing between categorical exclusion, EA, or EIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codifies factors and procedures to determine when an environmental document is required or when a categorical exclusion applies, consistent with statute and case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorical Exclusions (§1501.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and scope of categorical exclusions (CEs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses when actions may be categorically excluded, the role of 'extraordinary circumstances', and the possibility to adopt another agency's CE (per statutory provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental Assessments (§1501.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and process for preparing Environmental Assessments (EAs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains purpose of EAs to determine significance, whether an EIS is required, and to support Findings of No Significant Impact (FONSI) if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Findings of No Significant Impact (§1501.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for issuing a FONSI after an EA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies content and justification needed to document why an EIS is not required, consistent with concise and informative document principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead Agency (§1501.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Designation and responsibilities of a lead agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies criteria for lead, joint‑lead, and cooperating agencies and respective duties in preparing a single environmental document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperating Agencies (§1501.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Role and expectations for cooperating agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines when cooperating agency status is appropriate, how agencies should coordinate, and how expertise and authorities are used in reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public and Governmental Engagement (§1501.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for public involvement and engagement with governments and Tribes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires full and fair public engagement, early outreach, meaningful input opportunities for Tribal Nations, States, local governments, and affected communities, and effective communication strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines and Schedule for the NEPA Process (§1501.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations for setting and meeting timelines and schedules for NEPA reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs agencies to establish schedules and deadlines, tracking, and transparency mechanisms to improve efficiency and regulatory certainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic Environmental Documents and Tiering (§1501.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of programmatic documents and tiering to streamline analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides circumstances where programmatic EAs/EISs and tiering are appropriate to avoid duplication and improve efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by Reference Into Environmental Documents (§1501.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for incorporating material by reference in environmental documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows incorporation to avoid repetition but requires that incorporated material be reasonably available and summarized so the document remains informative and self-contained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Codification of 2023 GHG Guidance (Part 1502 preamble)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognizes guidance on consideration of greenhouse gas emissions and climate effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs EISs to consider GHGs and climate impacts consistent with CEQ's 2023 GHG guidance and prior CEQ guidance on analyzing climate‑related effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of an Environmental Impact Statement (§1502.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines purpose and role of an EIS in NEPA decisionmaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EISs provide detailed statements on environmental effects, alternatives, and mitigation to inform decisions and public participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation (§1502.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to implement procedures for preparing EISs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides practical steps, responsibilities, and coordination in EIS preparation, including adherence to CEQ standards and other legal obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoping (§1502.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and purpose of scoping in EIS preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoping identifies significant issues, determines scope of analysis, and engages stakeholders early to focus the EIS on relevant concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing (§1502.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Timing requirements for EIS preparation relative to agency decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EISs should be prepared early enough to inform decisions, with coordination to avoid premature decisions that would foreclose meaningful analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page Limits (§1502.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prescribed page limits for environmental impact statements and related documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes page limits to promote concise documents and reduce unnecessary verbosity while allowing flexibility where justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing (§1502.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for clear, concise, and effective writing in environmental documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages plain language, organization, use of summaries, and avoidance of unnecessary technical jargon to make documents accessible to decisionmakers and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft, Final, and Supplemental Statements (§1502.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for preparing draft, final, and supplemental EISs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies notice, comment, and response requirements for each stage and criteria for when supplemental EISs are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended Format (§1502.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested organizational format for EIS documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes cover, summary, purpose and need, alternatives, affected environment, environmental consequences, and appendices to ensure consistency and usability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover (§1502.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Content expectations for the cover of an EIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cover should include identifying information and make it easy to find key metadata (e.g., agency, project, date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary (§1502.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for an informative summary in an EIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary must concisely describe significant findings, alternatives, and recommendations so readers can quickly grasp major conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and Need (§1502.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to define and document purpose and need for proposed actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose and need should be grounded in the agency's statutory authority and reasonably narrow to allow a reasonable range of alternatives while not foreclosing meaningful options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternatives Including the Proposed Action (§1502.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for identifying and analyzing alternatives in an EIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require analysis of a reasonable range of alternatives, including the no‑action alternative, consideration of technically and economically feasible alternatives, and transparent rationale for alternatives eliminated from detailed study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affected Environment (§1502.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: What to include in the description of the affected environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the existing environmental baseline context necessary to understand potential effects, using reliable data and sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental Consequences (§1502.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for analyzing direct, indirect, and cumulative environmental effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze reasonably foreseeable effects, quantify where appropriate, disclose adverse effects that cannot be avoided, and evaluate mitigation measures and their effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of Scoping Information (§1502.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of scoping results in the EIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize scoping comments received, issues identified, and how scoping shaped the scope of analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete or Unavailable Information (§1502.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to handle incomplete or unavailable information in environmental analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe any incomplete information, its relevance, why it is unavailable, and how the agency addressed uncertainty in the analysis per NEPA principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology and Scientific Accuracy (Proposed §1502.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements to use sound methodologies and ensure scientific accuracy in environmental documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates professional and scientific integrity, use of reliable data and resources, and appropriate peer review or quality assurance for analyses informing decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inviting Comments and Requesting Information and Analyses (§1503.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: How agencies should invite public comments on EISs and request information/analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages proactive solicitation of useful information and analyses from the public and stakeholders to inform the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity of Comments and Information (§1503.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations for the specificity of public comments submitted on environmental documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs commenters to provide specific, substantive information and analyses to the extent possible to enable meaningful agency responses; explains that vague or general comments may limit the agency's ability to respond substantively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response to Comments (§1503.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for agency responses to public comments on EISs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires agencies to respond to substantive comments in a timely and reasoned manner in the final EIS or response document, explaining how comments were considered and any changes made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose (§1504.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Purpose of Part 1504 (Dispute Resolution and Pre-Decisional Referrals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets objectives for early dispute resolution and referral procedures to address interagency disagreements before final decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early Dispute Resolution (§1504.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and encouragement for early dispute resolution among agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages mechanisms to resolve disagreements early to avoid delays and clarify issues, including use of mediation and coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria and Procedure for Referrals and Response (§1504.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and process for referring disputes and agencies' required responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when and how disputes may be referred, timelines for responses, and standards for consideration by CEQ or other entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record of Decision in Cases Requiring Environmental Impact Statements (§1505.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for the Record of Decision (ROD) following an EIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RODs must document the agency's chosen action, alternatives considered, mitigation commitments, and monitoring/implementation plans as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementing the Decision (§1505.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for implementing decisions after NEPA review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses consistency of implementation with the EIS/ROD, mitigation, monitoring, and steps necessary to carry out the selected alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on Actions During NEPA Process (§1506.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits on taking actions that would preclude NEPA review or meaningful analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits agencies from taking actions that would limit reasonable alternatives or render NEPA review meaningless; ensures NEPA informs decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption (§1506.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for adopting another agency's environmental document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when and how an agency may adopt an EA or EIS prepared by another agency, including notice and publication requirements (e.g., EPA filing) if not previously a cooperating agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency Responsibility for Environmental Documents (§1506.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies' responsibilities for the content, quality, and legal sufficiency of environmental documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms agency accountability for ensuring documents meet NEPA requirements and are scientifically and legally defensible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology and Scientific Accuracy (§1506.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross‑part requirement to ensure methodological rigor and scientific accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinforces use of reliable data, peer review guidance, and information quality standards to support analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further Guidance (§1506.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority and expectations for issuance of additional NEPA guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows CEQ and agencies to issue further guidance on NEPA implementation topics as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposals for Regulations and Filing Requirements (§1506.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures related to proposing regulations and filing environmental documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers interactions between NEPA and rulemaking processes and specifics for submission/filing of documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of Agency Action (§1506.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for timing agency actions relative to NEPA analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures agency decisions are timed appropriately with the completion of environmental analyses and public participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergencies (§1506.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: How NEPA applies in emergency situations requiring swift agency action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides procedures and flexibility for NEPA compliance in emergencies while seeking to maintain environmental protection objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovative Approaches to NEPA Reviews (Proposed §1506.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourages innovative approaches to conducting NEPA reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits piloting or adopting novel procedures or technologies to improve efficiency, such as digital tools, consistent with statutory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective Date (§1506.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective date provisions for the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when the final rule (and individual provisions) takes effect (stated elsewhere as July 1, 2024 for this final rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance (§1507.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency obligations to comply with CEQ regulations and NEPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs agencies to develop procedures conforming to CEQ regulations and to ensure internal compliance mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency Capability To Comply (§1507.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for agencies to maintain capacity to implement NEPA procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses staffing, training, and resources needed for sound NEPA implementation and timely reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency NEPA Procedures (§1507.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements and expectations for agency‑specific NEPA implementing procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must prepare and update procedures consistent with CEQ regulations, tailored to statutory authorities and program contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency NEPA Program Information (§1507.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information agencies should maintain and share about their NEPA programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes transparency about NEPA processes, contact info, program descriptions, and ways to access documents and track reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (Part 1508) — Applicant (§1508.1(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and role of 'Applicant' for NEPA purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies who may be considered an applicant or project sponsor and their role in preparing documents or providing information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (Part 1508) — Categorical Exclusion (§1508.1(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of 'Categorical Exclusion'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains 'categorical exclusion' meaning, including that actions 'normally' covered may still require analysis if extraordinary circumstances exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (Part 1508) — Communities With Environmental Justice Concerns (§1508.1(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of communities with environmental justice concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to identify and prioritize consideration of effects on disadvantaged or overburdened communities in analyses and outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (Part 1508) — Cooperating Agency (§1508.1(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of 'Cooperating Agency'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies criteria for cooperating agency status and the expected contributions of such agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (Part 1508) — Effects or Impacts (§1508.1(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of 'Effects' or 'Impacts' for NEPA analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies scope (direct, indirect, cumulative) and foreseeability considerations for what constitutes an effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (Part 1508) — Environmental Assessment (§1508.1(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of 'Environmental Assessment'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains EA purpose to determine the significance of effects and whether an EIS is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (Part 1508) — Environmental Document (§1508.1(k))
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of 'Environmental Document'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers EAs, EISs, FONSIs, and other documents that inform NEPA decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (Part 1508) — Environmental Impact Statement (§1508.1(l))
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of 'Environmental Impact Statement'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes EIS as a detailed statement required for major Federal actions significantly affecting the human environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (Part 1508) — Environmental Justice (§1508.1(m))
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of 'Environmental Justice'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames environmental justice considerations and how they factor into NEPA analyses and outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (Part 1508) — Environmentally Preferable Alternative (§1508.1(n))
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of 'Environmentally Preferable Alternative'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to identify alternatives that best protect the environment among those analyzed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (Part 1508) — Extraordinary Circumstances (§1508.1(o))
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of 'Extraordinary Circumstances' that may preclude use of a CE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists factors that, if present, could cause an otherwise excluded action to have significant effects requiring further analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (Part 1508) — Finding of No Significant Impact (§1508.1(q))
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of FONSI and its role following an EA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies what a FONSI must demonstrate to justify not preparing an EIS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (Part 1508) — Human Environment or Environment (§1508.1(r))
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of 'Human Environment' or 'Environment'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies what environmental context and resources are encompassed by NEPA analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (Part 1508) — Joint Lead Agency (§1508.1(s))
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and role of 'Joint Lead Agency'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes when agencies jointly lead an environmental review and share responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (Part 1508) — Lead Agency (§1508.1(u))
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of 'Lead Agency' (see §1501.7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies selection criteria and responsibilities for a lead agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (Part 1508) — Major Federal Action (§1508.1(w))
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of 'Major Federal Action' triggering EIS requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines scope of actions that may require an EIS under section 102(2)(C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (Part 1508) — Mitigation (§1508.1(y))
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of 'Mitigation' for NEPA analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers avoidance, minimization, rectification, reduction/elimination, and compensation; references mitigation hierarchy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (Part 1508) — Notice of Intent (§1508.1(aa))
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and role of a Notice of Intent (NOI) in EIS scoping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NOI announces intent to prepare an EIS and initiates scoping and public involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (Part 1508) — Page (§1508.1(bb))
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition used to administer page limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies page counting conventions relevant to §1502.7 page limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (Part 1508) — Participating Federal Agency (§1508.1(dd))
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of 'Participating Federal Agency'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes agencies with special expertise invited to participate in NEPA processes without full cooperating agency status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (Part 1508) — Programmatic Environmental Document (§1508.1(ee))
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of 'Programmatic Environmental Document'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for program‑level analyses that inform subsequent tiered reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (Part 1508) — Reasonable Alternatives (§1508.1(hh))
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of 'Reasonable Alternatives' for alternatives analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets bounds for what constitutes a reasonable range of alternatives given the purpose and need and technical/economic feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (Part 1508) — Reasonably Foreseeable (§1508.1(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of 'Reasonably Foreseeable' relating to effects and future conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies how agencies should assess foreseeability when analyzing direct, indirect, and cumulative effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (Part 1508) — Scope (§1508.1(kk))
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of the 'Scope' of analyses in NEPA documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides how to set geographic, temporal, and topical bounds of analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (Part 1508) — Significant Effects (§1508.1(mm))
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of what constitutes 'Significant Effects' requiring an EIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides criteria to evaluate significance considering context and intensity of effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (Part 1508) — Tiering (§1508.1(oo))
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and use of tiering in NEPA reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains sequencing of programmatic and project‑level analyses to avoid redundancy and focus analysis where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory NEPA requirements (Section 102(2)(C)-(F) codified)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory requirements for environmental documents added/amplified by the Fiscal Responsibility Act and codified by the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EISs should discuss reasonably foreseeable environmental effects, reasonably foreseeable adverse effects that cannot be avoided, and a reasonable range of alternatives; agencies must ensure professional integrity of discussions, use reliable data, and describe technically and economically feasible alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 106: Determining the Appropriate Level of NEPA Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory clarification when an environmental document is required and exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that agencies must prepare environmental documents for final agency actions unless doing so would clearly and fundamentally conflict with other statutory duties or is nondiscretionary; codifies practices on CEs, EAs, and EISs and allows adoption of other agencies' CEs per section 109.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 107: Timely and Unified Federal Reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory direction to promote timely, coordinated NEPA reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codifies designations for lead/joint‑lead/cooperating agencies, promotes development of single environmental documents, allows project sponsor involvement in preparing documents, and prescribes page limits and deadlines to improve coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 108: Programmatic Document Reliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory rules on reliance on programmatic environmental documents without additional review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines timeframes and circumstances under which agencies may rely on programmatic documents for subsequent decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 109: Adoption of Another Agency's Categorical Exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Allows agencies to adopt categorical exclusions established by other agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies conditions and procedures for adopting another agency's CE consistent with statutory authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 111: Statutory Definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds or clarifies statutory definitions relevant to NEPA (referenced in Part 1508).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides statutory definitions to align regulatory definitions with statute and improve clarity for implementation.
